transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Cora Vekulman.
There's still a lot of surprise over Michigan Democratic Congresswoman Hailey Stevens' decision
to endorse Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers.
She revoked her endorsement of Democratic Senate candidate Abdul Al-Sayed yesterday.
Stevens lost the Michigan Senate primary to Al-Sayed earlier this year.
Their relationship had been testy.
Michigan Democratic Congresswoman Debbie Dingle had tried to bring Stevens and Al-Sayed back together
but was surprised to learn of Stevens' decision yesterday.
By the end of the week, it was just very clear to me that this whole thing had become a distraction.
I had told her that. I had been talking with others about many of these things.
I was shocked when I saw what happened on Sunday because I had been talking to her.
She spoke to NPR's morning edition.
President Trump has praised Stevens' endorsement of Rogers.
The President is spending the final days of the midterms imploring Republicans to vote in key races.
NPR's Stephen Fowler attended a rally yesterday in Dubuque, Iowa.
At his penultimate in-person event, Trump did what Trump normally does.
Speak at length about many topics, from touting his accomplishments in office to attacking Democrats
and defended high gas prices caused by the ongoing war in Iran.
To be honest, I thought it would go up much higher than it went up.
And, you know, I don't want to say because they'll say, "Oh, he thinks it's a very small price to pay for the security of this country."
Also in the nearly two-hour speech, Trump commented on Republican U.S. Senate nominee Ashley Henson's weight,
heckled protesters as "stupid" and promises to send Americans money if Republicans kept control of Congress, something he cannot do.
Stephen Fowler, NPR News, Dubuque, Iowa.
Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies appear to be stabilizing.
That follows last week's theft of more than $6 billion from the world's largest crypto exchange, Binance.
NPR's Anthony Kuhn reports from Seoul the FBI says North Korea was behind the hack.
Over the weekend, Binance resumed withdrawals, which were suspended after the hack.
Investors responded by withdrawing about $3.6 billion from their accounts.
That's a net outflow of about 2.1 percent of Binance's assets.
The FBI said in a statement Saturday that a hacking unit called Traitor Traitor was responsible for the heist.
The unit is under North Korean military intelligence, which oversees cyber operations.
North Korea has so far not commented on the matter.
President Trump said that if North Korea is indeed behind the hack, the administration will talk to Pyongyang about it.
But Pyongyang continues to say it's not interested in re-engaging with Washington.
Anthony Kuhn, NPR News, Seoul.
You're listening to NPR News.
Enrollment is now open for the Affordable Care Act marketplaces.
That includes HealthCare.gov.
These are for people who do not get health insurance through their jobs or don't qualify for public programs.
The Trump administration says fewer people are enrolled because they were ineligible or were "fantom."
Health experts say it's more likely that millions of people are not enrolling because they cannot afford the premiums anymore.
Republicans declined to extend extra money to keep premiums at a lower cost.
Doctors for Connecticut Democratic Senator Chris Murphy say he had a stroke on Saturday.
They say Murphy has been awake and alert.
They expect him to make a full recovery.
In motorsport, Formula One has a new world champion, and Piers Adam Bierne reports he's the youngest ever.
With his race engineer congratulating him as he crossed the finish line at the Mexican Grand Prix,
all Kimi Antonelli could do was cry tears of joy.
That's what it sounded like on Apple TV.
Antonelli is only 20 years old.
That makes him the youngest F1 world champion by some distance.
He's dominated this season in his Mercedes. Speaking right after getting out of the car,
it was clear that this was the moment he's been waiting for.
Antonelli is also the first Italian champion since 1953.
Adam Bierne, NPR News.

topics.text: Rep. Hailey Stevens revokes endorsement of Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and backs Mike Rogers
Trump rally in Dubuque, Iowa defends high gas prices and attacks Democrats during two-hour speech
FBI blames North Korean military intelligence hacking unit for $6 billion Binance crypto theft
Binance resumes withdrawals as crypto markets stabilize after record exchange hack
Enrollment opens for Affordable Care Act marketplaces; fewer enrollees amid premium affordability concerns
Sen. Chris Murphy suffers stroke, is awake and alert, expected to fully recover
Kimi Antonelli, 20, wins Formula One world championship at Mexican Grand Prix, youngest ever
